questions: Can you explain how statistical significance relates to effect size and practical importance, given your statement that "statistical significance is the same as saying the result has a large effect size"?
Could you walk me through what you mean when you say "failed to reject, that result would show the two methods are genuinely the same"?

What additional limitations or assumptions, beyond sample size, do you think are important for this study, considering your note that "Future research should also check whether the result holds in other academic settings"?
briefing: Based on the submission only (no practice conversation). The student correctly identified that the p‑value is the probability of observing a difference at least as large as the one found if the null hypothesis were true, and they appropriately rejected the null hypothesis at the 0.05 level: “With p = 0.03 and α = 0.05, we reject the null hypothesis.” They also noted a limitation about sample size and external validity: “One limitation worth noting is sample size… External validity is a concern any time a study is conducted in a single course at one institution.” However, the student conflated statistical significance with a large effect size and practical importance: “A finding being statistically significant is the same as saying the result has a large effect size and is practically meaningful.” This misinterpretation contradicts the rubric’s requirement to separate statistical from practical significance. The statement that failing to reject would show the methods are “genuinely the same” also misstates what a non‑significant result implies.
